messages.content: I need to start a Chicago trip for my aunt’s seventieth birthday. My spouse and I can go Friday, September 25, through Monday, September 28. Dinner is Saturday at 6:00 in Lincoln Square, and the family is meeting at the Art Institute at 10:30 Sunday morning.

I’ll build this for two adults sharing one room from Denver. Before I compare combinations, what matters more on Friday: getting in early enough for the informal family gathering, or keeping the airfare down? Also, do you know roughly when that gathering starts?

It is loose, probably drinks and snacks around 5:30 at my cousin’s place near Lincoln Square. There is a less expensive nonstop after work and a more expensive afternoon flight. I want to see whether the earlier arrival buys us enough useful time.

The useful comparison is between a 1:20 p.m. Denver departure arriving O’Hare at 4:47 p.m. and a 5:35 p.m. departure arriving at 8:58 p.m. Both are nonstop. The afternoon round trip is $846 for two; the evening option is $642. From O’Hare to Lincoln Square, allow about 45–65 minutes by car on Friday afternoon and roughly 60–75 minutes by Blue Line plus a transfer. The 4:47 arrival might put you at the gathering around 6:15 with checked luggage, so it does not really deliver a full afternoon. The evening flight misses it altogether.
What are the Monday returns paired with those? We do not need to stay late Monday, but I do not want a dawn airport run.

The $846 pairing returns from O’Hare at 12:45 p.m., reaching Denver at 2:28 p.m. The $642 pairing returns at 1:50 p.m. and reaches Denver at 3:33 p.m. There is also a middle combination: Friday at 3:05 p.m., arriving 6:31 p.m., with the 1:50 p.m. Monday return for $734 total. Realistically, that gets you to Lincoln Square around 7:45, so you might catch the end of the gathering but should not count on it.
Then the middle one is poor value. Compare the early and late Friday choices together with hotel areas. I was thinking Lincoln Square, River North, or near the Loop.

Lincoln Square is best for Friday and Saturday, but Sunday requires a 35–50 minute CTA trip to the Art Institute, and Monday’s O’Hare transfer is less direct. River North splits the difference: about 25–35 minutes to Saturday dinner, 15–20 minutes to the museum, and straightforward access toward O’Hare. The Loop is easiest for Sunday morning but quieter at night and about 30–40 minutes from Lincoln Square. For only one Lincoln Square obligation that requires punctual arrival, River North is the strongest overall base.
Show me actual three-night hotel choices in River North and the Loop. One room for two adults, including taxes. We do not need anything elaborate.

Three workable refundable totals are: Fairfield Inn & Suites Chicago Downtown/River North at $711, including breakfast; AC Hotel Chicago Downtown in River North at $768, without breakfast; and Club Quarters Hotel Central Loop at $639, without breakfast. Fairfield is about a five-minute walk from the Grand Red Line station, which gives you a simple ride north for dinner. Club Quarters is a short walk from the Art Institute but adds time Saturday and leaves fewer nearby options late Sunday.
How do those look when airfare and airport transportation are included? Assume we use the train from O’Hare unless the arrival makes that unreasonable.

With the evening flight, Blue Line transfers both ways, and the Fairfield, the working total is about $1,363: $642 airfare, $711 hotel, and roughly $10 in CTA airport fares for two. Club Quarters brings that to about $1,291. With the afternoon flight, those totals become about $1,567 at Fairfield or $1,495 at Club Quarters. The afternoon arrival still permits rail, but you would need to leave your bags at the hotel and continue to Lincoln Square; reaching the gathering before about 6:30 would be optimistic.
Could we go directly from O’Hare to my cousin’s, then check in afterward? We would each have a carry-on roller.

You could. A taxi or rideshare from O’Hare directly to Lincoln Square is likely $45–$70 before tip and could take 45–70 minutes. With a 4:47 p.m. arrival, you might reach the gathering around 5:50–6:20 if the flight and baggage exit are smooth. The drawback is bringing two rollers into the gathering and then traveling downtown later. Adding that ride makes the afternoon-flight premium roughly $250 over the evening-flight plan, not just the $204 fare difference.
That is too much for an informal gathering. Let’s take the evening flight. Now compare Fairfield and Club Quarters specifically for Saturday dinner and Sunday museum timing.

From Fairfield, leave around 4:55 p.m. Saturday. Walk to Grand, take the Red Line to Fullerton, then the Brown Line to Western; with the final walk, the trip is usually 35–45 minutes and leaves a cushion before 6:00. A car may be 25–40 minutes but is more traffic-sensitive. Sunday, leave Fairfield around 9:55 for a 20-minute walk or short bus ride to the Art Institute. From Club Quarters, Saturday takes about 40–50 minutes by CTA, so leave near 4:45. Sunday’s museum walk is only about 8–10 minutes, letting you leave at 10:10.
And for O’Hare Monday? Also, is breakfast at Fairfield early enough that we are not paying for something we cannot use?

For the 1:50 p.m. Monday flight, leave Fairfield around 10:25 a.m. Walk to the Clark/Lake Blue Line station and allow about 55 minutes to the terminal area, giving you comfortable airport time. From Club Quarters, Monroe Blue Line is closer, so departure around 10:35 works. Fairfield serves breakfast from 6:30 to 9:30 on weekdays and 7:00 to 10:00 on weekends, so you can use it all three mornings without compressing either scheduled event.
Fairfield sounds better for the weekend even though it costs more. Before we settle, is the room there one king or two beds, and what is the cancellation cutoff?

The $711 refundable rate is for one king room for two adults. Two queens are available at $747 total. The refundable rate can be canceled without penalty until 11:59 p.m. local time on Wednesday, September 23; after that, the charge is one night plus tax. The quoted amount includes hotel taxes, and no destination fee is listed.
One king is fine. Put together the exact combination we have narrowed this to, but do not book yet. I need the total and the main movements.

Selected combination, still unbooked: Friday, September 25, nonstop Denver to Chicago O’Hare departing 5:35 p.m. and arriving 8:58 p.m.; Monday, September 28, nonstop O’Hare to Denver departing 1:50 p.m. and arriving 3:33 p.m. Airfare for two is $642. Fairfield Inn & Suites Chicago Downtown/River North is $711 including taxes for three nights in one king room, with breakfast included and free cancellation through 11:59 p.m. Chicago time September 23. Air plus hotel is $1,353; adding estimated CTA airport fares for two brings the working total to $1,363.
Give me the practical schedule too. I want to make sure the hotel does not create a problem for either family commitment.

Friday, take the Blue Line from O’Hare toward downtown, transfer or walk from Clark/Lake, and expect to reach the Fairfield around 10:20–10:40 p.m. Saturday, leave the hotel about 4:55 p.m. for the Red and Brown Lines to Western, aiming to reach the Lincoln Square dinner by 5:40. Sunday, finish breakfast by about 9:30 and leave at 9:55 for the Art Institute, arriving around 10:15 for the 10:30 meeting. Monday, check out and leave around 10:25 a.m. for the Blue Line to O’Hare. That allows roughly two hours at the airport before the 1:50 p.m. departure. The River North hotel works cleanly for both commitments; the only decision left is whether to purchase the selected flights and refundable room.
